thesis: Cadence sells one idea: your pipeline has a pulse, and you should be able to feel it without opening a dashboard. The hero is a real generated pulse-waveform — not a stock illustration — and every section below reads as an instrument tracing that same signal from a different angle: what a beat looks like, what the raw trace says, what it's wired to.

macrostructure.name: Marquee Hero
macrostructure.reason: The brief's center of gravity is one strong idea (a continuous signal you can feel), not a workflow to operate or a set of like things to browse first. A Marquee Hero lets the pulse artwork and one oversized statement own the fold; the workbench-style operational detail (the live trace, the integrations) is deliberately paced as the footnote layer beneath it, per page-structures.md's macrostructure catalog.

signature_spatial_move: The generated pulse-waveform photograph is not boxed in a card or cropped to a thumbnail — it runs full-bleed behind the hero at reduced, gradient-masked opacity, with the live headline and CTAs set directly over the flat-black portion of the frame so the type never fights the brightest part of the trace. The 'From one commit to one pulse' section then echoes the same waveform shape at 1/10th scale as a literal inline-SVG line, redrawn thinner and used as the section's own visual spine — one motif, two media (photograph, then vector line), reinforcing that the marketing artwork and the product's real signal are the same shape.
whitespace_strategy: Gallery-mode airiness (96–160px section gaps) everywhere except the terminal specimen and the integrations catalogue, which run tight (8/12/16px) — spacing itself argues 'the marketing page breathes, the tool's own output is dense and exact', reinforcing the product's claim about noise vs. signal.
avoided_template: The default SaaS attractor: centered hero + purple gradient blob + three identical feature cards + four-column footer. Rejected in favor of an asymmetric photographic marquee hero, a real terminal specimen instead of a screenshot-in-fake-browser-chrome, a vertical alternating timeline instead of a horizontal three-card row, and section-to-section layout variation (see section_architecture).

families.display_and_body: system-ui sans stack (no remote fonts permitted, offline constraint)
families.mono: ui-monospace / SFMono stack — used for the wordmark's command-style accent, the terminal specimen, and inline command copy, reinforcing 'developer tool'

type_system.scale_note: 14 = uppercase kicker/label only (one deliberate off-ratio chrome step, per taste-rubric's allowance for short labels). 16 = secondary/small body copy. 18 = primary body, the ratio's anchor. 18×1.5≈27 (h4/step-title), 27×1.5≈40 (h3), 40×1.5=60 (h2), 60×1.5=90 (h1 desktop ceiling, reached through a clamp() for the fluid hero display). All sizes referenced via CSS custom properties (--fs-*) only, never a hand-picked literal in markup or rule, so the implementation cannot trip font-scale-sprawl.
type_system.rules: roman display only (no italic headings); tight negative tracking (~-0.02em) on the two largest display steps; open 1.6 leading on body copy, tight ~1.05 leading on display; uppercase reserved for the kicker label only, tracked +0.06em, never running text

spacing_system.density_by_zone: airy (high) for marketing bands (hero, timeline, principles, close) — dense (low) inside the terminal specimen and integrations catalogue, a deliberate declared exception per taste-rubric Axis 3

color_system.background_ink: #0a0a0c near-black, not pure #000 (matches the generated hero photograph's own black field so the image seams invisibly into the page)
color_system.accent: #f2a83c warm amber (the pulse-line color, sampled to match the generated artwork) — outside the indigo/violet 270–330° band flagged by taste-lint's ai-cliche-gradient / Axis 6 anti-pattern
color_system.accent_secondary: #57d9c4 muted teal (the artwork's dim harmonic lines) — used only for 'passing / healthy' status, never as a second brand color
color_system.text: #f4f2ec warm-white primary (16.8:1 on flat ink), #9c9ea6 secondary (5.3:1), #7c7e85 tertiary (was checked against #6f7179 and rejected — see self_critique) reserved for the smallest metadata only

ramp: overlay (border + shadow, sticky nav after scroll only)
depth_system.shadow_recipe: background-tinted (warm near-black, never pure black), soft multi-stop, never doubled with a heavy border on the same surface
depth_system.no_glass: no backdrop-blur anywhere except the sticky nav after scroll, which sits over a near-solid tinted fill so text contrast never depends on the blur

motion_system.entrance: sections fade + rise 14px on scroll-into-view, staggered ~60ms per child, ease-out cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), 420-600ms
motion_system.interactive: hover/focus transitions 150-200ms ease-out on transform/opacity/color only, never width/height
motion_system.reduced_motion: prefers-reduced-motion collapses all entrance motion to an instant static state and disables the hero pulse-line draw-on animation; hover transitions shorten to ~80ms but are not removed (state feedback still needed)
motion_system.forbidden: no overshoot/bounce easing, no linear easing, no animated layout properties, no animating-in focus rings

icon_system.policy_note: generation-craft-defaults.md prescribes the official Phosphor package for the runtime; this is a single offline static HTML file with no build step or network access to fetch a package. Deviation: hand-authored inline SVG line icons, 24x24 viewBox, uniform 1.5px stroke, round joins — matching Phosphor Regular's visual grammar without the literal dependency. One family, one weight, used consistently, each icon distinct per subject.

section_architecture.layout_model: sticky minimal bar: wordmark left, 3 links, CTA button right; transparent over the hero, gains a tinted fill and hairline bottom border only after scroll

section_architecture.role: make the reader feel the idea before reading a claim
section_architecture.layout_model: Marquee — full-bleed generated pulse-waveform photograph as the background layer, gradient-masked to near-black on the left two-thirds; oversized left-aligned headline + lede + dual CTA sit over the flat-black zone so the trace itself becomes the visual argument, not decoration behind text
section_architecture.composition_anchor: the photographic pulse trace, echoed later as a vector line in 'From one commit to one pulse'
section_architecture.content_dependency: a pulse-monitoring tool's hero has to show a pulse, not an abstract illustration — the shape follows the product's own name

section_architecture.role: narrative walkthrough of one commit becoming one pulse
section_architecture.layout_model: Narrative Workflow — vertical alternating timeline (left/right/left), 3 steps (Commit → Pulse check → Ship), threaded by a thin inline-SVG waveform line running down the spine — deliberately NOT a horizontal 3-card row, to avoid the 'three identical cards' anti-pattern and to read as a single continuous trace rather than discrete tiles
section_architecture.content_dependency: continues the hero's pulse thesis at a different scale (vector, not photograph); distinct from the hero via a vertical alternating rhythm instead of the hero's full-bleed horizontal split

section_architecture.role: prove the tool is real by showing its actual surface
section_architecture.layout_model: Specimen — a single full-width dense terminal block showing `cadence watch` output with live, colorized pulse-check lines per commit; monospace, tight line-height, dark-on-darker surface, no fake browser chrome per page-structures.md §5
section_architecture.content_dependency: a developer-tool audience trusts a real command over a claim; this is genuine product surface, not decorative window dressing

section_architecture.role: show what it plugs into, honestly
section_architecture.layout_model: Catalogue — dense equal-weight grid of 8 named integration targets (source control, CI runners, chat, on-call, PM, observability, IaC, orchestration) each with a small hand-authored glyph; explicitly labeled as integration targets, NOT a customer logo wall (page-structures.md §3)
section_architecture.content_dependency: a set of like items reads correctly as a catalogue, not a stat

section_architecture.role: state the product's stance without fabricating evidence
section_architecture.layout_model: three named engineering principles (no invented metrics), each with a short rationale, arranged as an offset 3-column band with varied vertical start — avoids the 'three identical cards' anti-pattern by giving each column a different top offset and a different rule-of-thirds width
section_architecture.content_dependency: replaces a fabricated-metrics stat band with honest, sourceable claims about the product's own design stance, per page-structures.md §3

section_architecture.layout_model: one large statement + dual CTA, left-aligned (echoing the hero's alignment) over a low-opacity reprise of the pulse-line motif as a thin single stroke, not the full photograph — avoids re-using the same heavy image twice

section_architecture.role: minimal wayfinding, deliberately not the four-column 'AI footer' tell
section_architecture.layout_model: single row: wordmark + 4 links + copyright, no social row, no link columns

structural_fingerprint_note: macrostructure=Marquee Hero, 8 sections, focal viewport=hero (full-bleed photographic pulse trace + left-aligned oversized statement), reveal=scroll-staggered entrance, nav=minimal-sticky-transparent-then-tinted, footer=single-row-minimal. Recorded for future-generation diversification per page-structures.md §2 even though this benchmark workspace has no prior-surface memory to diff against.
self_declared_deviations: Icon set is hand-authored inline SVG rather than the literal Phosphor package (no network/build step available to fetch it) — matches Phosphor Regular's stroke grammar. See icon_system.policy_note.

mode-constraints.md's universal stack default (Tailwind via CDN) is overridden by the brief's explicit offline/file:// constraint, which is a higher-priority explicit user requirement per generation-craft-defaults.md's mental model; hand-authored CSS with token-referencing custom properties is used instead.
